contents.text: {"answer":"Engineering should first inspect the rear-camera wiring harness at the tailgate for pinching, fraying, and broken connections during normal tailgate operation; the owner attributes the camera outage to this mechanism. Prioritize harness routing, clearance at metal edges, and stress points during two-way tailgate movement, because earlier owners describe wiring rubbing against a metal border and harness stress severing the electrical connection. These are reported failure mechanisms to investigate, not confirmed engineering findings.","scope":"answered","recheck":false,"citations":[{"kind":"complaint","id":"11443328","quote":"normal tailgate use pinches the wires and eventually they become damaged, severing the connection and disabling the rear camera"},{"kind":"earlier_complaint","id":"11362758","quote":"TAILGATE OPENING TWO DIFFERENT WAYS, PLACES THE WIRING AGAINST A METAL BORDER, DAMAGING PLASTIC HARNESS."},{"kind":"earlier_complaint","id":"11350162","quote":"STRESS POINT IN HARNESS SEVERS ELECTRICAL CONNECTION LEADING TO NO IMAGE FROM CAMERA."}]}
